title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents
why: Selects web-agent memories by predicted decision utility instead of semantic relevance, tested on WebShop.
mechanism: Web-agent memory: counterfactual interventions estimate each memory's decision utility; a distilled estimator keeps memories under a token budget without changing the policy or requiring more environment interaction.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: on ALFWorld, 86.57 SR@50 at a 500-token historical-memory budget vs 65.67% for BM25; also evaluated on WebShop; analysis says utility is sparse, state-dependent, and poorly captured by semantic relevance.

title: Outcome-Mass Alignment: Controlling Length-Dependent Trajectory Influence in Multi-Turn LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning
why: Aligns multi-turn agent RL so longer failed trajectories are not over-weighted, including on WebShop-SOL.
mechanism: Training: Outcome-Mass Alignment computes outcome statistics over unique source trajectories and controls aggregate objective mass after token-level reduction, without redesigning the base optimizer's credit assignment, ratios, or clipping.

title: The Value of Thinking: Learning When to Reason in Hybrid Decision Models
why: Learns when a single model should spend reasoning tokens, including on the MiniWoB GUI agent venue.
mechanism: Planning/compute: a hybrid decision model uses one frozen backbone and a self-routing block that estimates the value of full autoregressive thinking versus a no-token forward pass; CDPO trains the router from episode-level returns on agentic tasks.

why: Adds personal adapters and online routing over general skills for agents on WebShop and ALFWorld.

title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
why: Compares decision models as actor, judge, or teacher; JEV teaching lifts WebShop and ALFWorld policies.
mechanism: Training signal: the same decision model is tested as actor, post-hoc judge, and RL teacher; judging whether each action helped (after the episode) is used to teach a policy even when the model acts poorly.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: as a teacher, JEV raises a Qwen2.5-1.5B GRPO policy from 72.8% to 82.9% success on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop; actor vs judge contrast also reported on ALFWorld.
